title: CEAT's Profit Fell 96% in One Quarter. Arnab Banerjee Refused to Cut Prices.
summary: CEAT lost ₹20 crore in late 2021 while rivals stayed in profit. Under CEO Arnab Banerjee it went premium, hit a record ₹697 crore profit and held price.

title: Tech Mahindra's Margin Hit an All-Time Low. Mohit Joshi Made His Target Public.
summary: Tech Mahindra's margin hit an all-time low of 4.7% in 2023. Mohit Joshi set a public 15% target for FY27, and by September 2026 the margin was 14.8%.

title: 56 of 100 Indians Had Never Heard of Daikin. Kanwaljeet Jawa Changed That.
summary: In 2009, 56 of 100 Indians had not heard of Daikin. Kanwaljeet Jawa took it from ₹440 crore to ₹10,361 crore with dealers and local factories. The board lesson.

title: Paytm Lost 36% in Two Days. Vijay Shekhar Sharma Said: We Should Have Done Better.
summary: Paytm's shares fell 36% in two days after the RBI's 2024 action. Vijay Shekhar Sharma admitted mistakes, kept UPI alive and made ₹552 crore profit in FY26.

title: COVID Took Nearly 90% of BookMyShow's Revenue. Ashish Hemrajani Kept Building.
summary: COVID cut BookMyShow's revenue from ₹701 crore to ₹74 crore. Ashish Hemrajani cut hard, kept building, and FY25 profit hit ₹192 crore. The lesson for boards.

title: Ola Called Old Scooters Boring. Sudarshan Venu's TVS Beat It With Dealers.
summary: Ola Electric won the launch hype in 2021. Sudarshan Venu built TVS's EV business through dealers, and in FY26 TVS sold 3,41,471 e-scooters to Ola's 1,64,294.

title: Rajesh Magow Became MakeMyTrip's CEO 43 Days Before India Stopped Flying. Here Is What He Did.
summary: Weeks after Rajesh Magow became Group CEO, Covid cut MakeMyTrip's revenue by 95%. He cut his own pay first, kept building, and FY26 bookings topped $10 billion.

title: Kalyan Jewellers Listed 15% Below Its IPO Price. T S Kalyanaraman Then Grew It Fourfold.
summary: Kalyan Jewellers listed 15% below its issue price in 2021. T S Kalyanaraman grew it through franchise showrooms to ₹35,743 crore of revenue in FY26.

title: Mahindra Lost Its SUV Spot to Kia by 156 Cars. Rajesh Jejurikar Asked What It Stood For.
summary: In FY21 Mahindra fell to fourth in SUVs, 156 units behind Kia. Rajesh Jejurikar reset the brand, and in FY26 Mahindra sold a record 6,60,276 SUVs.

title: Birla Opus Came for Asian Paints With ₹10,000 Crore. Amit Syngle Refused a Price War.
summary: Birla Opus entered paints with ₹10,000 crore and lower prices. Amit Syngle kept spending on the brand, and Asian Paints' volumes grew 12.4% by early 2026.

title: Honda Walked Away From Hero in 2010. Pawan Munjal Built His Own Engines and Stayed No. 1.
summary: In 2010 Honda ended its 26-year Hero Honda partnership. Pawan Munjal built Hero's own engineering, and in FY26 Hero still outsold Honda in India.

title: Albinder Dhindsa: Zomato Bought His Struggling Startup. Now He Runs Zomato's Parent.
summary: In 2022 investors gave Blinkit zero value. Albinder Dhindsa stayed, scaled 10-minute delivery, and in 2026 Blinkit made a ₹102 crore quarterly profit.

title: Ajay Bijli's Sales Fell 92% in a Year. Now 150 Million People Buy His Tickets.
summary: In FY21 PVR's revenue fell 92% and it lost ₹748 crore. Ajay Bijli cut fixed costs 63%, raised ₹1,600 crore and merged with INOX: 150 million tickets in FY26.

title: Vikram Mehra Took Saregama From ₹19 Crore to ₹206 Crore With Songs From the 1950s
summary: In FY14 Saregama's music revenue fell 18.5% and its MD quit. Vikram Mehra turned the old catalogue into Carvaan and streaming: ₹684 crore of music in FY26.

title: Shailesh Chandra Took Over Tata's Cars at Their Low Point. Sales Are Now Nearly 5x.
summary: Tata Motors sold 5,676 cars in India in March 2020. Shailesh Chandra bet on EVs and the Punch, and in FY26 Tata sold 6,31,387 cars, nearly five times FY20.

title: Saugata Gupta Bought Founders, Not D2C Teams. Then He Kept Marico Out.
summary: Marico's CEO bought Beardo, Just Herbs and Plix instead of building digital brands, and left the founders alone. They now run above ₹1,100 crore a year.

title: Sanjiv Puri Let Go of ITC's Hotels. ITC Still Made ₹20,286 Crore.
summary: In 2023 Sanjiv Puri moved ITC's hotels into a separate company and kept 40% despite investor pressure. In FY26 ITC Hotels paid its first dividend.

title: Rajiv Bajaj Walked Away From Scooters. Then He Rebuilt the Chetak Name.
summary: In 2009 Rajiv Bajaj took India's most famous scooter maker out of scooters. A decade later Chetak came back as an EV, and by June 2026 it had sold 8 lakh.

title: Jayen Mehta Took Amul to America Without Exporting a Litre of Milk From India
summary: Amul crossed ₹1 lakh crore in brand turnover in FY26 and will never list. Jayen Mehta took it to America on farmer-owned milk, not on capital markets.

title: R C Bhargava: Maruti's Share Hit a 13-Year Low. It Still Sold a Record 24 Lakh Cars.
summary: Maruti's market share hit a 13-year low of 39.26% in FY26, yet it sold a record 24.22 lakh vehicles. R C Bhargava, 91, told analysts not to harp on share.

title: Ashok Vaswani: The RBI Banned Kotak on His 115th Day. He Had It Lifted.
summary: On Ashok Vaswani's 115th day as Kotak Mahindra Bank CEO, the RBI barred online onboarding. He fixed the problem he inherited; the curbs lifted on day 409.

title: Falguni Nayar: Nykaa's Stock Fell, Its Profit Grew Nearly Tenfold
summary: Nykaa listed 79% above its issue price, then fell out of India's top 100 companies. Falguni Nayar kept growing it: profit went from ₹21 crore to ₹204 crore.

title: Varun Alagh: When Honasa Fell 40%, He Bought More
summary: Mamaearth's parent Honasa fell 40% to ₹223 after its first listed loss. Varun Alagh bought shares twice, ₹50 crore the second time. By Sept 2026: near ₹480.

title: Gaurav Singh Kushwaha: BlueStone's First Profit Came Without a Turnaround
summary: BlueStone listed below its ₹517 issue price after a ₹219 crore loss. Gaurav Singh Kushwaha took FY26 to a ₹26 crore profit on ₹2,441 crore revenue.

title: Puneet Chhatwal: He Grew the Taj by Owning Less of It
summary: Taj Hotels had lost money for seven straight years when Puneet Chhatwal took over. He raised ₹4,000 crore mid-pandemic and took IHCL's profit past ₹2,000 crore.

title: Gopal Vittal: He Let 40 Million Customers Leave Airtel on Purpose
summary: When free mobile data cut Airtel's profit 76.5% in a year, Gopal Vittal let 40 million low-spenders go and built the network for those who would pay more.

title: M P Ahammed: How a Coconut Trader Built India's Largest Jeweller
summary: M P Ahammed traded coconut and spices for 12 years, opened one jewellery shop in Kozhikode in 1993, then sold debentures in the Gulf to grow it to 445 stores.

title: Anish Shah: The Outsider Who Fixed Mahindra's ₹5,200 Crore Problem
summary: Mahindra's profit fell 98% in the year to March 2020. Anish Shah, its first non-family group CEO in 75 years, hit the five-year RoE target in eighteen months.

title: Noel Tata: The Job He Didn't Get, and the One He Built Instead
summary: In 2011, Noel Tata was passed over for chairman of Tata Sons. He built Zudio into 963 of Trent's 1,286 stores and in 2024 became chairman of Tata Trusts.

title: Costs Were Rising Everywhere. Sameer Khetarpal Cut Domino's Prices Anyway.
summary: Sameer Khetarpal held Domino's India prices flat and backed its own delivery fleet. Profit rose 190% by the September 2025 quarter, helped by a one-time gain.

title: He Ran India's Biggest Luggage Company. Then He Bought the Rival One-Tenth Its Size.
summary: Sudhir Jatia bought 56.55% of Safari Industries for ₹29 crore in 2011. Sales have grown from ₹70 crore to over ₹2,047 crore, and market share from 2% to 23%.

title: Venu Nair Took the Job Nobody Wanted at Shoppers Stop. He Turned It Around in About a Year.
summary: Venu Nair took the top job at Shoppers Stop in 2020 with revenue heading for a 44% fall, kept a ₹450 crore savings drive on track and turned net-cash in a year.

title: Bharat Puri Heard About the Cadbury Worms From TV News. He Fixed It in Three Months.
summary: Bharat Puri led Cadbury India through the 2003 Dairy Milk worm crisis. Festive sales fell 30 percent. He rebuilt trust and sales recovered within six months.

title: Verghese Kurien Packed His Bags to Leave Anand. He Stayed Fifty Years and Built Amul.
summary: Verghese Kurien came to Anand in 1949 planning to leave. He stayed fifty years and built Amul, now owned by 3.6 million farmers and past ₹1 lakh crore.

title: Everyone Said Royal Enfield Was Finished. Siddhartha Lal Asked for Two Years.
summary: Siddhartha Lal took over Royal Enfield at 26, as his family prepared to shut it. He fixed the machine first. It sold over 10 lakh motorcycles in FY25.

title: C K Venkataraman: How Tanishq Fixed Years of Being Wrong About India
summary: C K Venkataraman ran Tanishq's jewellery division from 2005 to 2019 and helped build India's leading organised jewellery business: over ₹46,000 crore in FY25.

title: Ramesh Chauhan Sold Thums Up to Build Bisleri From Scratch
summary: Ramesh Chauhan sold India's No. 1 cola brand to Coca-Cola in 1993, then rebuilt his fortune on bottled water nobody wanted to pay for. A category lesson.

title: Sunil D'Souza Turned Down Tata's FMCG Job, Then Built It From Tea and Salt
summary: Sunil D'Souza said no to leading Tata's consumer business because it lacked direction. That was why Chandrasekaran wanted him. A lesson in the unclear brief.

title: Suresh Narayanan: The MD Who Walked Into the Maggi Ban
summary: 38,000 tonnes of Maggi were destroyed. Suresh Narayanan took the MD job that same year and rebuilt Nestle India to ₹20,000 crore. How he ran the crisis.

title: Shailesh Jejurikar: P&G's First Indian-Origin CEO in 187 Years
summary: Shailesh Jejurikar joined P&G in 1989 from IIM Lucknow and never left. On January 1, 2026 he became its first Indian-origin CEO in 187 years.

title: Sudhir Sitapati: Why He Left HUL's Safest Seat for Godrej
summary: Sudhir Sitapati led HUL's Horlicks merger, then left to run Godrej Consumer. What nearly five years at a smaller, messier company reveal about leadership.

title: Sanjiv Mehta: The HUL Leader Who Never Forgot Bhopal
summary: Sanjiv Mehta grew HUL's value more than 4x, closed the GSK merger, and doubled women in leadership. What Bhopal taught him about running a boardroom.

title: Refused to Blink: The Boardroom Lesson Behind Marico's War With Hindustan Lever
summary: In 1999, Hindustan Lever tried to kill Parachute. Marico's founder refused a buyout and fought on four fronts. What the decision to fight actually took.
